question: How should the operating system, GPU driver, container runtime and Kubernetes be tuned so GPUs are not starved by host-side bottlenecks?
contributions: Checklist of host OS tuning (NUMA, pinning, hugepages, swap, scheduler, C-states, allocators)
GPU driver/runtime settings (persistence, MPS, MIG, clocks, ECC, OOM)
Container and Kubernetes tuning (Container Toolkit, GPU Operator, Topology Manager, host networking, QoS)

limits: Almost all speedup figures are unsourced ranges ('it's possible to see') with no hardware, workload or baseline.
Chapter is training-centred; inference is addressed only in side remarks (THP, persistence, MIG).
Says MIG changes need a reset in one place and 'without rebooting' in another.
Says 'As of this writing' for MIG disabling P2P/NVLink and Kubernetes lacking I/O isolation; these may date.
MIG example arithmetic (45 GB for two 2g.45gb slices) conflicts with Table 3-1.
practices: Pin each process and its memory to the GPU's NUMA node with numactl --cpunodebind/--membind or taskset, and reapply in DataLoader workers (NUMA section).
Use pinned memory (pin_memory=True, non_blocking=True) and raise ulimit -l to unlimited for large pinned buffers.
Enable THP for throughput-bound training; disable it (transparent_hugepage=never) or use madvise for latency-sensitive inference.
Set vm.swappiness=0 and keep swap at zero; use cgroups v2 for memory and CPU pinning.
Set CPU governor to performance and limit deep C-states.
Pin device interrupts to cores on the device's NUMA node; disable or customise irqbalance.
Tune jemalloc or tcmalloc through MALLOC_CONF / TCMALLOC_* variables.
Enable persistence mode (nvidia-persistenced) on all GPUs at boot.
Use MPS for several small jobs that leave slack, MIG for isolation, and neither for large multi-GPU jobs.
Lock clocks (nvidia-smi -lgc) only for benchmarking; otherwise leave auto-boost on.
Keep ECC enabled for serious AI workloads.
Keep the driver and MIG configuration loaded across jobs.
Match host driver to container CUDA version (R580 for CUDA 13.x, R525 for 12.x); use NGC base images.
Use bind mounts rather than the overlay filesystem for datasets and checkpoints.
Enable Kubernetes Topology Manager (best-effort, restricted or single-numa-node) and the latest device plugin and GPU Operator.
Use hostNetwork: true for performance-sensitive multinode jobs; install RDMA device plugin and enable GPUDirect RDMA.
Request whole nodes; set requests == limits for Guaranteed QoS, or avoid tight memory limits to dodge the OOM killer.
Do not use MIG for large distributed training or inference spanning GPUs.
